linh_nguyen.md:
- The resume's current-job bullets copy the JD's "What you will do" list: all nine duties, in the JD's order, in nearly the JD's words, which is what you get when a resume is written from the posting rather than from memory of the work
- The resume names its employers only as "Leading Fintech Company" and "Global Technology Solutions Firm", with no team sizes, numbers or incidents, so there is nothing here that could be checked
- Phone screen: ask about one specific Kubernetes upgrade they ran and what went wrong; someone who did the work will have a story
review: yes
soojin_kim.md:
- The resume's "Key Qualifications" section copies the JD's "What we are looking for" list word for word, so it tells you what the posting asked for, not what this person has done
- The resume's "Nice to Have" section copies the JD's "Nice to have" section, heading and all, which is a posting section, not a resume section
- The resume describes the current job as "You will design, build and operate...", which is how the JD addresses an applicant, not how a person describes their own work; that phrasing usually means text was pasted from the posting
- The resume names its employers only as "Fintech Startup" and "Technology Company", so the work history cannot be verified as written
review: yes
petr_ivanov.md:
- The resume's opening "Mission" paragraph is the JD's "About the role" paragraph reworded into the first person, so the candidate's stated goal is the employer's text
- The resume's "Summary of Qualifications" walks through the JD's "What we are looking for" list in the JD's order, which is unlikely to happen by chance when someone writes from their own history
- The resume gives its two earlier jobs one line each with unnamed employers, so there is no track record to compare the claims against
review: yes
jordan_harris.md:
- The resume's current-job bullets restate the JD's "What you will do" list with one word swapped per bullet (the JD's "Design, build and operate" becomes the resume's "Architected and operated") in the same nine-bullet order, so the structure is the posting's even though the words differ
- The resume names its employers as "Confidential Financial Services Company", "Enterprise Software Organization" and "Technology Consultancy", and gives no numbers anywhere, so nothing can be checked
- Phone screen: ask which company it was and how much transaction volume it handled; a vague answer would confirm the concern
review: yes
arjun_singh.md:
- The resume's current-job bullets follow the JD's "What you will do" list in order and wording, with a percentage added to the end of each, so the results look measured but the underlying claims are still the posting's
- Every percentage in the resume is a round number (80%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 90%, 100%, 300%) and every uptime figure is 99.99%, which is what invented metrics tend to look like
- The resume's employers and dates look real, but no number is tied to a specific system, incident or time period, so the specifics may be decoration rather than evidence
- Phone screen: pick two of the percentages and ask how they were measured; real ones come with a story, invented ones do not
review: yes
marcus_chen.docx:
- Flagged only because most of the JD's acronyms appear in the resume, which is expected for someone who has this stack; the resume's wording is its own and names tools the JD never mentions
- The resume's detail is specific enough to check (14 AWS accounts, about $2B in payment volume, a 31% cost cut with the steps that got there), which is the opposite of what a resume written from a posting looks like
- Nothing suggests the resume's wording came from the JD
review: no
